**Why an AI Agent Forgets After a Long Session, and What a Summary Does About It**

**Scene 1 – A person at a desk, handing a helper a growing stack of notes and tasks.**
Imagine you hire a helper for a big project. All day, you talk. You share goals, decisions, and small details. The helper remembers it all, and the work goes well.

**Scene 2 – The stack of paper climbs until it tips over the edge of a small desk.**
An AI agent works like this too. It handles long jobs in one running conversation. But the model reading that conversation has a limit, called its window. It can only hold so much at once.

**Scene 3 – The desk is full. A hand sweeps the pile toward the edge.**
When the conversation grows too big for that window, something has to give. The agent can't simply keep everything.

**Scene 4 – The long pile is squeezed into a single neat page, labeled "Summary."**
So the conversation is compressed into a summary. The agent puts the long history aside and keeps working from that short page.

**Scene 5 – Close-up: a sticky note with a detail slips off the pile and vanishes.**
Here's the catch. Any detail that didn't make it into the summary is gone. The agent won't know it ever existed. That's why a long session can seem to forget a choice you made hours ago.

**Scene 6 – A reviewer holds up the summary and asks the agent questions, ticking boxes.**
So how do we know a summary is good? We test it. We ask the agent questions about the old work: What did we decide? Why? What's left to do? If it answers correctly, the summary kept what mattered.

**Scene 7 – The helper smiles at a tidy desk, one clear page in front of them.**
A good summary lets the agent keep going without losing the thread. A weak one leaves holes.

**Closing card – Title text fades in: "Check the summary, keep the memory."**
Long memory isn't magic. It's a summary, and it's only as good as what it keeps.
